c.tagline: Gothic cathedral city on the Seine where Monet painted and Joan of Arc died

taxi.fareNote: Official taxis are metered with a visible rooftop light; fixed supplements apply for night, Sunday, and station pickups

emergency.note: 112 works for all emergencies; 17 reaches police directly and 15 reaches the SAMU medical service

avoid.reason: Mind bags around the rail station and in crowds near the cathedral; left-bank streets are quiet and deserted after dark.

hood_desc: Vieux Rouen (the historic center) is a dense maze of half-timbered medieval houses around the Gros-Horloge and Rouen Cathedral, packed with shops, cafés, and the Place du Vieux-Marché where Joan of Arc was burned at the stake.
Rive Gauche, across the Seine, is a modern district of offices, the Panorama XXL and Historial Jeanne d'Arc museum, and riverside walkways, with fewer tourists and cheaper rents.
Saint-Marc is a lively, slightly bohemian neighborhood built around its namesake outdoor market, popular with students and known for an easygoing, multicultural feel.
Jouvenet, near the Musée des Beaux-Arts, is a quiet, well-heeled residential quarter of grand 19th-century townhouses just north of the old center.
Saint-Sever, on the left bank, centers on a large shopping mall and transit hub, offering practical, budget-friendly lodging within a short tram ride of the cathedral.

Hôtel Kyriad Rouen Centre Saint Sever

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout France.

transit.pay: Astuce card or app tickets, single fare covers bus/tram transfers for about an hour
transit.note: Rouen's TEOR guided busway and single tramway line cover the compact city well; the historic center itself is best explored on foot

train: Direct SNCF trains from Paris Saint-Lazare, about 70-90 minutes
bus: FlixBus and BlaBlaCar Bus connect Rouen to Paris and other French cities

tip.r: Service is included by law (service compris); rounding up or leaving small change for good service is appreciated but not obligatory
